articles.content: Pratika Rawal produced a match-winning performance for Railways, while Shreyanka Patil continued to strengthen her case for an India comeback as the Super Eight stage of the Senior Women's T20 Trophy Elite began in Ahmedabad on Saturday.Rawal played a magnificent knock of 86 off just 52 balls to help Railways chase down Mumbai's 158-run target in a thrilling encounter. With Railways struggling at 735 at the halfway stage, the India opener joined hands with Sneh Rana to revive the chase, stitching together a crucial 70-run partnership.Although Rawal eventually departed, Rana held her nerve, remaining unbeaten on 37 off 30 balls and sealing a three-wicket victory with a boundary when Railways needed one run off the final two deliveries.The knock will be encouraging for Rawal, who will be looking to carry her form into the upcoming WPL season with UP Warriorz. Her ability to hold the innings together under pressure was particularly impressive, especially with Railways needing a substantial contribution after losing half their side.SHREYANKA IMPRESSES VS BARODAShreyanka, meanwhile, continued her impressive run for Karnataka against Baroda. The off-spinning all-rounder returned figures of 319 in four overs as Baroda were bowled out for 137. She also chipped in with an unbeaten 10 off six deliveries as Karnataka completed a five-wicket victory in just 13.3 overs.The performance comes at an important time for Shreyanka, who was not part of India's home T20I series against Zimbabwe and was subsequently left out of the squads for the multi-format tour of South Africa. Despite registering two successive five-wicket hauls earlier in the tournament, the 23-year-old was overlooked for the senior team.However, she has received an opportunity to push for a return after being named in all three India A squads for the upcoming home series against England A. Shreyanka will feature in the T20, one-day and multi-day teams, with the series beginning on November 30.MANDHANA, VRINDA HEADLINE OTHER PERFORMANCESThere were several other notable performances on the opening day. Jemimah Rodrigues, who recently returned to competitive cricket after recovering from a hamstring injury, had already made a strong statement in the tournament by smashing 107 off just 47 balls against Pondicherry. However, she could not carry that form into the Super Eight opener, managing just five runs against Railways as Mumbai suffered a narrow defeat.Smriti Mandhana, meanwhile, endured a difficult outing for Maharashtra against Andhra. The India captain scored 30 off 33 balls, hitting two fours and a six, but struggled to accelerate as her team posted 1616. Maharashtra eventually secured a 48-run victory, restricting Andhra to 1139. Anuja Patil contributed 31 off 21 balls and picked up two wickets.Vrinda Dinesh also made a strong statement ahead of her WPL commitments. The RCB recruit smashed 49 off just 19 balls at a strike rate of 258, helping Karnataka chase down Baroda's total. Niki Prasad also contributed with 31 off 17 deliveries.Elsewhere, Arundhati Reddy conceded 29 runs in her two overs for Baroda, while Radha Yadav went wicketless. For Maharashtra, the victory over Andhra provided a positive start to their Super Eight campaign.- Ends

articles.title: Hurt Suryakumar Yadav vows to break the door down for India comeback - India Today
articles.summary: Hurt Suryakumar Yadav vows to break the door down for India comeback India Today
articles.content: Suryakumar Yadav is not ready to give up on his India career just yet. After spending a difficult few months out of the national team, the Mumbai batter has found fresh motivation to fight his way back, making his intentions clear with a stunning knock in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy on Saturday.Returning to action for Mumbai after being left out of India's T20I plans, Suryakumar smashed a 21-ball 60 against Hyderabad in their tournament opener. His explosive innings helped Mumbai chase down a target of 173 in just 13.1 overs, sealing a seven-wicket win with 41 balls to spare.Speaking after the match, the former India captain admitted that being overlooked following India's T20 World Cup triumph had hurt him. Having expected to continue representing the country after being part of a historic campaign, Suryakumar said the disappointment had now become a source of motivation."After winning the World Cup, you naturally expect that you will play after the IPL or whenever India's first series takes place. Because you have won a major tournament, and winning an ICC event is not easy, especially on home soil, something nobody had achieved before," Suryakumar was quoted as saying by PTI."But the selectors must have had their reasons and must have thought things through before taking that decision. But yes, I was hurt. If you don't feel sad or hurt, how will you turn that into passion, and how will you play with that passion? That is what I am trying to do now," he added.'I WILL HAVE TO BREAK THE DOOR DOWN'Suryakumar believes the setback has reignited the hunger that drove him to establish himself in the Indian team. The 35-year-old is now determined to make the most of his opportunities in domestic cricket and earn another shot at international cricket."The same hunger I had earlier to play for India, when I used to score runs after returning to domestic cricket, has come back again. If I want to play for India again, I will have to break the door down once more. All right, let's do it," he said.The Mumbai batter also expressed gratitude to Mumbai Cricket Association president Ajinkya Naik for appointing him captain of the state side during a challenging phase of his career.Suryakumar said the decision reflected the faith and respect the association continued to have in him, even when he was no longer part of India's plans."To stand by me during that difficult period, show support and make me the captain of the state team again - he could have chosen someone else. He had that option, but the responsibility, love and respect he has given me mean a lot. I will always remain grateful and humble for that," he said.ADAPTING TO THE NEW T20 GAMESuryakumar also spoke about the evolving demands of T20 cricket, with teams increasingly targeting totals of 250 and 260. He believes batters must maintain their attacking intent beyond the powerplay and continue taking calculated risks through the middle overs."After that, when we bat between overs seven and 15, it is important to maintain the same intensity and intent, even when playing for India. If we have to score 250-260, then that is what we have to do, and I am trying to follow that approach," he said."The 'high-risk, high-reward' game in the middle overs has always been part of my batting. But now I am trying to understand how I can take even more risks and hit more boundaries and sixes because T20 cricket has become a format dominated by boundaries and sixes," he added.With his India comeback firmly on the agenda, Suryakumar will be keen to build on his impressive start in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. Consistent performances for Mumbai could strengthen his case for a return, as he looks to turn his renewed hunger into another opportunity to represent the country.- Ends

articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur wants India to recreate World Cup magic at Champions Trophy - India Today
articles.summary: Harmanpreet Kaur wants India to recreate World Cup magic at Champions Trophy India Today
articles.content: The celebrations following India's historic Women's ODI World Cup triumph may have faded, but the memories of that unforgettable campaign continue to inspire the team. Harmanpreet Kaur is hoping the players can draw from that experience when they return to familiar territory for the inaugural Women's Champions Trophy in February 2027.India's World Cup-winning campaign remains a landmark moment for women's cricket in the country. Harmanpreet believes the prospect of playing another major ICC tournament at home offers the team an opportunity to create more special memories, particularly with Mumbai among the host cities."Whenever we talk about winning the ODI World Cup, not just me but all the players still get goosebumps because that was the biggest achievement for us. The Champions Trophy is also in Mumbai, and hopefully, we will repeat the same history, create the same moment and play with the same mindset," the World Cup-winning captain told the media during an Omaxe Estates event on Saturday."Whenever we have played in Mumbai, we have always done well. Hopefully, this time too, when we get the opportunity, we will do our best," she added.SOUTH AFRICA TOUR TO PROVIDE IDEAL PREPARATIONIndia will have an important assignment before the Champions Trophy, with a multi-format tour of South Africa scheduled for December. The visitors will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is, giving the team valuable match practice ahead of the global competition.Harmanpreet feels the series could play a significant role in helping India build momentum and confidence."The Champions Trophy is a very big tournament for all of us. I am sure the South Africa tour before that will help us prepare well. Hopefully, we will carry a lot of confidence from there and perform well in the Champions Trophy," she said.The former India captain also highlighted how the Women's Premier League (WPL) could help the players get accustomed to the conditions. With matches scheduled at venues that will also host the Champions Trophy, India could benefit from that familiarity."The WPL is a platform that has always given us a lot of confidence," she said."It is great that before the Champions Trophy, we will get to play in a very good tournament at the same venues. We will be playing in Baroda and Brabourne, and then in Mumbai for the Champions Trophy. I think that will also give us a lot of confidence going into the tournament."The inaugural six-team Women's Champions Trophy, which will be played in the T20I format, will take place in Mumbai and Vadodara from February 14 to 28, 2027.- Ends

articles.title: PSL team brutally trolled for mocking India after Pakistan lose U19 Asia Cup final - India Today
articles.summary: PSL team brutally trolled for mocking India after Pakistan lose U19 Asia Cup final India Today
articles.content: Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchise Karachi Kings were brutally trolled on social media after Pakistan suffered a one-wicket defeat to India in the U19 Asia Cup 2026 final. The franchise's attempt to mock the Indian team following Pakistan's strong performance with the ball backfired spectacularly after India's youngsters pulled off a remarkable chase to lift the trophy.Karachi Kings shared a post on their social media account featuring a mock chat conversation, with the caption, "This chat has been restricted by Rizwanullah". The screenshot showed messages suggesting that Vineeth VK and Arjun Rajput had left the chat, seemingly referring to Pakistan pacer Rizwanullah's impressive performance in the final. Rizwanullah had indeed made an impact with the ball. He picked up three wickets, dismissing Vineeth for 24 and Rajput for 16 when India were 172 for three in 31 overs during their chase of 338. He also removed Aryan Savsani to finish with figures of 353 in his 10 overs.However, Karachi Kings' celebration proved premature. India recovered from a difficult position to chase down the target, finishing at 339 for nine in 50 overs. The franchise's attempt to take a dig at the Indian youngsters quickly backfired, with Indian cricket fans flooding social media with reactions and trolling the PSL side for celebrating before the match was over. Rizwanullah, who represents Karachi Kings in the PSL, made his tournament debut last season. He featured in two matches and picked up three wickets. The young pacer, however, enjoyed a much more productive campaign in the U19 Asia Cup 2026, finishing as the joint-highest wicket-taker with 14 wickets.MANAL, MOHIT TURN THE GAME AROUNDIndia's chase had received a solid foundation from openers Aaryavir Sehwag and captain Lakshya Raichandani. Sehwag scored 58 off 61 balls, while Raichandani anchored the innings with 80 off 101 deliveries. However, Pakistan fought back with regular wickets, leaving India struggling at 252 for eight.Just when Pakistan appeared to have the match under control, Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva produced a stunning counterattack. The duo added 57 runs for the ninth wicket in just 5.5 overs, bringing India back into the contest. Manal smashed 47 off 32 balls, while Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, hitting three sixes and five fours.Manal eventually departed, but Mohit continued to keep India's hopes alive alongside Chigurupati Venkata. With eight runs needed in the final over and three required off the last ball, Mohit smashed a boundary off Ahmed Hussain to seal a sensational one-wicket victory.The triumph was India's ninth U19 Asia Cup title. They reclaimed the crown after missing out on the trophy in the previous three editions, with Bangladesh winning in 2023 and 2024 before Pakistan lifted the title in 2025.- Ends

articles.contentHindi: Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchise Karachi Kings were brutally trolled on social media after Pakistan suffered a one-wicket defeat to India in the U19 Asia Cup 2026 final. The franchise's attempt to mock the Indian team following Pakistan's strong performance with the ball backfired spectacularly after India's youngsters pulled off a remarkable chase to lift the trophy.Karachi Kings shared a post on their social media account featuring a mock chat conversation, with the caption, "This chat has been restricted by Rizwanullah". The screenshot showed messages suggesting that Vineeth VK and Arjun Rajput had left the chat, seemingly referring to Pakistan pacer Rizwanullah's impressive performance in the final. Rizwanullah had indeed made an impact with the ball. He picked up three wickets, dismissing Vineeth for 24 and Rajput for 16 when India were 172 for three in 31 overs during their chase of 338. He also removed Aryan Savsani to finish with figures of 353 in his 10 overs.However, Karachi Kings' celebration proved premature. India recovered from a difficult position to chase down the target, finishing at 339 for nine in 50 overs. The franchise's attempt to take a dig at the Indian youngsters quickly backfired, with Indian cricket fans flooding social media with reactions and trolling the PSL side for celebrating before the match was over. Rizwanullah, who represents Karachi Kings in the PSL, made his tournament debut last season. He featured in two matches and picked up three wickets. The young pacer, however, enjoyed a much more productive campaign in the U19 Asia Cup 2026, finishing as the joint-highest wicket-taker with 14 wickets.MANAL, MOHIT TURN THE GAME AROUNDIndia's chase had received a solid foundation from openers Aaryavir Sehwag and captain Lakshya Raichandani. Sehwag scored 58 off 61 balls, while Raichandani anchored the innings with 80 off 101 deliveries. However, Pakistan fought back with regular wickets, leaving India struggling at 252 for eight.Just when Pakistan appeared to have the match under control, Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva produced a stunning counterattack. The duo added 57 runs for the ninth wicket in just 5.5 overs, bringing India back into the contest. Manal smashed 47 off 32 balls, while Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, hitting three sixes and five fours.Manal eventually departed, but Mohit continued to keep India's hopes alive alongside Chigurupati Venkata. With eight runs needed in the final over and three required off the last ball, Mohit smashed a boundary off Ahmed Hussain to seal a sensational one-wicket victory.The triumph was India's ninth U19 Asia Cup title. They reclaimed the crown after missing out on the trophy in the previous three editions, with Bangladesh winning in 2023 and 2024 before Pakistan lifted the title in 2025.- Ends

articles.summary: Watch: Tricolour, celebrations and payback as India stun Pakistan in Asia Cup U19 final India Today
articles.content: Brief Scores: India U19 (3399 in 50 overs) beat Pakistan U19 (3379 in 50 overs) by 1 wicket in Al Amerat. (Mohit Ulwa 49*, Lakshya Raichandani 80; Kavya Patel 468)The U19 Asia Cup final had it all. There was drama, emotions running high, and an Indian team that celebrated wildly after securing a sensational win over arch-rivals Pakistan.IND vs PAK, U19 Asia Cup Final: HighlightsMohit UIva's whirlwind knock ensured the win and as the final ball of the match went past the boundary, the entire Indian team made its way onto the field. It was a moment of payback for the Indian team as they got revenge for the loss they suffered during the group stage.Mohit showed off why he was the iceman in the contest, having arms aloft, almost like Jude Bellingham as he was enveloped by his teammates.Then came the moment to give it back to the Pakistan team as some of the members celebrated in front of wicketkeeper Hamza Zahoor. The celebrations didn't end there as the Indian players sent a message to the entire Pakistan team and fans and sent them off the field.Mohit was wrapped in the tricolour like a hero and the team soon made their way to the Indian fans section, who kept cheering on for them all the way till the last ball.HOW THE MATCH UNFOLDEDIndia were facing a big task as Pakistan posted 337 runs in the first innings. India made a steady start, thanks to fifties from Aaryavir Sehwag and Lakshya Rajesh Raichandani.However, the momentum was missing and India was soon under pressuree to get the run-rate up.At one point, India looked dead and buried in the contest inside a packed Al Amerat Cricket Ground on Saturday, November 14. India had just lost captain Lakshya Rajesh Raichandani and Anvay Dravid in consecutive deliveries in the 37th over. Then the miracle happened.Manal Chauhan led the fightback and he was joined Mohit Ulva, and the duo left Pakistan absolutely stunned. Chauhan fell in the 48th over and the hopes were high for Pakistan as they could sense victory. But then Mohit turned everything on its head with 49 not out.- Ends

articles.title: Indian sports wrap, November 14: Atiqa Mir only Indian chosen for FIA’s women driver development program - Sportstar
articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 14: Atiqa Mir only Indian chosen for FIA’s women driver development program Sportstar
articles.content: CHENNAI MOTORSPORT Atiqa Mir only Indian chosen for FIA’s women driver development program Indian racing prodigy Atiqa Mir is among nine drivers chosen worldwide in the junior category for the FIA Girls On Track Rising Stars program for 2026. Atiqa is one of the youngest drivers chosen for the world body FIA backed initiative aimed at promoting and developing young women drivers at the grassroots level. She is also is the only Indian named in the age 12-14 junior category. Girls On Track was launched by the FIA in 2018. Atiqa’s selection follows a string of impressive performances in the Champions of the Future Academy (COTFA) championship and the FIA Karting World Championship where she finished sixth in the opening race. She had dominated the COTFA round in Greece earlier this year. “In just over two weeks, nine talented racers will head to Cremona Circuit (in Italy) for three-day training camp designed to sharpen their skills and help take their racing to the next level,” read a note from the FIA Women in Motorsport Commission. The other drivers picked by the FIA in the junior category are Lina Salamanca from France, Sofia Calderon from Costa Rica, Cora Moore from Britain, Anna Regina Franco Rodriguez from Mexico, Lily Rizk from Egypt, Kira Maistrenko from Ukraine, Annais Orelana from Chile and Emily Grace Hamer from Australia. Atiqa, the first Indian to be backed by the Formula 1 Academy, is currently taking part in the final round of COTFA series in Franciacorta, Italy. - PTI CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship, Round 2: Photo finish, last-lap battles and dramatic comebacks mark opening day DTS Racing’s Augustine Boby edged Meco Racing’s Shatveer Shetty by just 0.032 seconds in the F1300 Novice Cup, while Dark Don Racing’s Mehul Agarwal and Team Performance Racing’s Deepak Ravikumar pulled off late overtakes to claim victories in LGB Formula 4 and Indian Junior Touring Cars, respectively on the opening day of Round 2 of the CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship at the Kari Motor Speedway in Coimbatore. Vadodara’s Kabir Sahoch continued his winning run in the Amateur class, surviving two red-flag interruptions and a six-lap restart to finish 0.979 seconds ahead of Saurav Sanjay Dey in the Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup. In the JK Tyre Levitas Cup, Mumbai’s Pratik Sonawane completed a double in the Gentleman class with two pole-to-flag victories. In the Super Saloon categories, Arka Motorsports’ Arjun Narendran won the Indian Super Touring Cars race by 7.288 seconds after holding off an early challenge from Arjun Balu, while Team N1 Intervalve’s Biren Pithawalla snatched second from Balu in the closing moments. In the Indian Touring Cars, Team Performance Racing’s Balaprasath A won ahead of Ramcharan Chandran and Vidyaprakash Damodaran. - Team Sportstar GOLF Women’s Pro Golf Tour, 14th leg: Jasmine Shekar wins second title of season, holds off Vani and Ridhima Jasmine Shekar managed to extend her overnight one-shot advantage to two shots and claim her second title of the season in the 14th leg of the Women’s Pro Golf Tour at the Rambagh Golf Club in Jaipur on Saturday. The 21-year-old Jasmine, who hails from Bengaluru, took the lead into the final round, held her nerve to card 1-over 71 and finish ahead of two of the most experienced players in India, Vani Kapoor (72) and Ridhima Dilawari (74). In a week when no player had an under par total, Jasmine aggregated 5-over with rounds of 74-70-71, while Vani Kapoor (75-70-72) was 7-over for three days and Ridhima (74-71-74) was 9-over at the challenging course. Shweta Mansingh (74-75-71) was fourth at 10-over for three days. Jasmine has been one of the consistent performers on the domestic circuit, more so this year. She had opened her 2026 campaign with a victory in the first leg in Mumbai and had since come close to adding to that tally, finishing runner-up at both DLF Golf & Country Club and Jaypee Wishtown. At Rambagh, she finally converted another opportunity into a title. She became the third player after Ridhima and Vani to win more than once in 2026. The result was particularly satisfying because the challenge came from two players who have enjoyed outstanding seasons. Vani and Ridhima had shared second place going into the final round, and both had the experience and form to put Jasmine under pressure. Vani had also arrived in Jaipur on the back of an impressive runner-up finish at the Hero Women’s Indian Open, the best result of her Ladies European Tour career. Jasmine, however, did just enough to give herself a chance and convert it into a fine win. The Rambagh Golf Club course, a par-70 layout, proved a demanding test throughout the week. Scoring was difficult, with players finding it hard to get into red figures. In fact, there was just one under-par round in the entire tournament, a superb four-under 66 by Tvesa Malik. Despite producing the lowest round of the week, Tvesa could finish only tied seventh, underlining the difficulty of the conditions. She was tied seventh with Ananya Datar, a first-round co-leader with amateur Ojaswani Saraswat (74), who was tied fifth alongside Riya Jadon. Jasmine played solid on the final day and was steady. She had two bogeys on the second and fifth, which put her in danger. However she had a birdie on the Par-3 sixth followed by five straight pars. Another birdie on the 12th was followed by four more pars. She looked set for the win as she stayed ahead of Vani. She could even afford a bogey on the 17th. Vani had two bogeys and no birdies on the front and on the back nine she had just one birdie, but she also bogeyed the 18th. A birdie on the 18th could have got her into a play-off, but it was not to be and she lost by two. For Vani, second place was another strong result in a season in which she has remained one of the leading forces on the domestic circuit. The experienced professional has already won twice this year and finished runner-up on three occasions before the Jaipur event. Her recent performance at the Hero Women’s Indian Open had further underlined her ability to compete at a higher level. Ridhima, meanwhile, continued to add valuable points to an already impressive season. The Order of Merit leader has been the most consistent player on the tour, with four victories before this event, and her third-place finish keeps her firmly in position to win the Merit honours. Though the result at the Jaipur leg looked close, this week belonged to Jasmine, who never let things get out of hand and the next event, which will be the final one for 2026, will be held at Noida Jaypee Wishtown, which had also hosted the sixth leg, which was won by Ridhima and Jasmine was second. - PTI Top golfers for PGTI event at Digboi Top Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) golfers such as Honey Baisoya, Om Prakash Chouhan, Akshay Sharma and Rashid Khan will be seen in action in the ₹1 crore Indian Oil Servo Masters event to be held at the Digboi Golf Links course, Assam, from November 17 to 20. The tournament week will begin with the pro-am event on Sunday. - Team Sportstar SNOOKER Six Indians advance to final stage of World Snooker Championships Kamal Chawla outplayed Laxman Rawat to book his spot in the final stage of the IBSF World Snooker Championships in Indore on Saturday. On song from the get-go, Chawla scored a crushing 4-1 victory in the third round of the first event. A little later, five more Indian cueists booked their spots in the second stage with contrasting victories. After the two split the first two frames of the best-of-seven-frame clash, Chawla shifted gears to leave Rawat gasping in his wake. He made a brilliant 133 break in the third frame, and after winning the fourth on the black, the 47-year-old came up with a sizzling break of 108 to power into the second stage. In the clash between two promising cueists, Kreishh Gurbaxani came good when it mattered to score a gritty 4-2 win over the red-hot Rayaan Razmi. Gurbaxani, who played two seasons on the pro tour, got going after losing the first two frames. A fine break of 78 in the third gave him the confidence, and he played a solid game to keep Razmi in check, winning the next three frames, which could have gone either way. S Shrikrishna, a former World champion in the shorter format, came into his own after a slow start against fellow Indian Pushpender Singh. After losing the first frame, Shrikrishna had runs of 81, 84 and 120 on his way to a 4-1 victory. Piyush Kushwaha, Ranveer Duggal and Digvijay Kadian were other Indians to advance to the final stage. - PTI MORE SPORTS Ladakh Marathon adds 180 km Siachen Ultra to race roster The Ladakh Marathon is taking high-altitude distance running to new extremes with the launch of the Siachen Ultra, conceived as the world’s toughest ultra-running challenge across 111 miles (180 km) of the Trans-Himalayan ranges. The race will traverse the mountain landscape of the Karakoram and Himalaya, taking field of highly experienced ultra runners from Warshi Village near Siachen to Leh, via the Nubra region and Khardung La at 17,618 ft (5,370 m). articles.title: Australia and India strengthen sports partnership in Tamil Nadu - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Australia and India strengthen sports partnership in Tamil Nadu The New Indian Express
articles.content: CHENNAI: Building on the Australia-India Roadmap for Sports Collaboration, which was announced earlier this year in July, the Australian Consulate-General, Chennai welcomed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Basketball Australia and the Basketball Federation of India (BFI), marking a significant step forward in sports cooperation between the two nations. The MoU, which was signed on Friday, establishes a framework for collaboration in coach, player and referee development, high-performance sport, governance, sports integrity, and community engagement. Under the agreement, the two organisations will work together to create development pathways for athletes, coaches and officials, facilitate knowledge exchange, promote friendly competitions and exposure visits, and strengthen diaspora engagement.Aadhav Arjuna, president of the BFI, and Matt Scriven, Chief Executive Officer of Basketball Australia, formalised the partnership on behalf of their respective organisations. Matt Scriven said, "We are proud to announce this partnership with the Basketball Federation of India and to support basketball's rapid growth in one of the world's most exciting emerging basketball markets." Aadhav Arjuna said, "Basketball has a unique power to unite societies, transcend cultures and bring communities together. This partnership between Basketball Australia and the Basketball Federation of India is more than an MOU; it is a shared commitment to strengthening India's basketball ecosystem, nurturing future generations and building a pathway towards making India a basketball powerhouse in Asia and, one day, on the world stage. May the dribble become the heartbeat of every aspiring Indian basketball player, and the dream of representing India a reality." Witnessing the virtual MoU signing, Australian Consul-General in Chennai, Silai Zaki said, "Today's MoU reflects the growing momentum in the Australia-India sporting relationship. With the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad and the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games on the horizon, there has never been a better time for Australia and India to team up and build stronger sporting links." The growing sports partnership between Australia and India will be on full display in Chennai this December. Jindal’s letter also contains the signatures of 25 other DDCA members, while Saluja has made a separate appeal. We thank Star Cement for their continued support and look forward to building on what we started together last season,” said Nildeep Mondal, the league CEO. Star Cement is the first title sponsor of the competition and extends the partnership, which started this year in March. - Team Sportstar Golf WPGT, 14th leg: Jasmine grabs sole lead with closing birdie; Vani, Ridhima and Durga in contention Jasmine Shekar produced a steady par 70, capped by a birdie on the closing hole, to take the outright lead after the second round of the 14th leg of the Women’s Professional Golf Tour at the Rambagh Golf Club on Friday. Jasmine, who opened with a 74, moved to a 4-over total of 144 and took a one shot lead into the final round. She was leading the experienced duo of Vani Kapoor (75-70) and Ridhima Dilawari (74-71), who, between them, have won six titles this season. Also tied for second with Kapoor and Dilawari was Durga Nittur (73-72) at 5-over 145. Overnight leaders Ananya Datar (71-75) and amateur Ojaswini Saraswat (71-76) slipped to fifth and sixth. Jasmine had three bogeys in the first six holes and then birdied the 8th, 14th and 18th to claw back to even par. Kapoor bogeyed the seventh and got back that shot on the 14th as scoring continued to be challenging at the Rambagh Club. Ridhima, meanwhile, followed her opening 74 with a one-over 71. She had an encouraging start to the round, including a birdie on the second. She dropped shots on the fifth and the seventh and then had one birdie and one bogey on the back nine for a 71. Durga also remained firmly in the hunt. After an opening 73, she carded a 72 to join Vani and Ridhima in second place. Her opening nine was particularly solid, with a 35, although a two-over back nine prevented her from taking a share of the lead. The second round also saw the first-round leaders lose ground. Ananya Datar, who had set the pace with a one-over 71 on Thursday, slipped to a five-over 75 and dropped to fifth at 146. She is now two shots behind Jasmine but remains close enough to mount a challenge. Amateur Ojaswini Saraswat also had a difficult day after beginning with a 71. She carded a six-over 76 to move to sixth at 147, three shots off the lead. Riya Jadon was in seventh place with rounds of 74-74, while Lavanya Jadon and Shweta Mansingh shared eighth at 149. Further down, Mannat Brar, Sneha Sharan, Amandeep Drall, Shagun Narain and Khushi Khanijau were tied for 10th at 150. -PTI

articles.title: KPMG sets up sports tech hub to unlock India’s $40-bn sports opportunity by 2030 - The Hindu
articles.summary: KPMG sets up sports tech hub to unlock India’s $40-bn sports opportunity by 2030 The Hindu
articles.content: Bengaluru KPMG in India opened its Sports Technology Hub, a platform designed to help sports organisations in the country accelerate digital transformation, unlock new growth opportunities and build future-ready sporting ecosystems. The initiative is expected to bring together emerging technologies, industry expertise, and practical use cases to address evolving business and operational challenges in the sports industry. As the sports industry continued to evolve, organisations were increasingly leveraging technology to enhance fan experiences, improve athlete performance and strengthen commercial outcomes, KPMG officials said, adding, ``However, fragmented data, legacy infrastructure, operational inefficiencies and rising expectations for personalised experiences continue to hinder innovation.’’ The Sports Technology Hub in Bengaluru aims to address these challenges through practical solutions that sports organisations can evaluate and adopt. The hub was officially inaugurated by Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India, and P. T. Usha, President of the Indian Olympic Association, here on Friday. Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India, said, “Realising India’s potential in sports calls for innovation across the entire sports value chain. Our sports technology hub aims to bring industry expertise and technology together to help reshape how a sport is played, managed and experienced. As India strengthens its position on the global sports stage, technology will be central to building a more competitive, connected and future-ready sports ecosystem.” According to Prasanth Shanthakumaran, Partner and Head of Sports Sector, KPMG in India said, the hub showcases a range of technology-driven solutions, including AI-powered fan engagement platforms, smart stadium and venue management, athlete performance analytics, computer vision-based training and match insights, digital ticketing and loyalty solutions, and sponsorship measurement tools. It also incorporates capabilities in predictive maintenance, cybersecurity, sustainability and generative AI-enabled content creation to help sports organisations optimise operations and unlock new commercial opportunities. “The Sports Technology Hub brings together cutting-edge technologies such as AI, advanced analytics, computer vision, and digital platforms to address some of the most pressing challenges facing the sports industry today,’’ added Mr. Shanthakumaran. By showcasing practical, outcome-driven solutions, we aim to help sports organisations innovate faster, improve performance, and create more engaging experiences for fans, athletes, and partners, he further said. Designed as a collaborative platform, the Sports Technology Hub is expected to bring together sports federations, leagues, clubs, technology providers, startups and other industry stakeholders to explore and scale innovative solutions.

articles.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday highlighted India's rapid progress in astronomy, astrophysics and space technology, emphasising that scientific advancements and space exploration must ultimately serve humanity.Speaking in Mysuru after inaugurating COSMOS-Mysuru, India's first LED Dome Planetarium, Modi said India's space programme has consistently focused on improving the lives of its people."Humanity first" has been the guiding principle of India's space missions, the Prime Minister said, pointing to how satellite technology is being used for applications ranging from disaster warnings to railway operations and public safety.Highlighting India's achievements in space, Modi said the country has made rapid progress in astronomy and astrophysics, with new telescopes being installed and ambitious scientific missions expanding its capabilities. PM Modi watch a visual at the newly inaugurated Mysore planetarium. (Photo: PIB)He cited Chandrayaan-3's historic landing near the Moon's south pole, the Aditya-L1 mission becoming India's first dedicated space-based solar observatory and ISRO's Space Docking Experiment (SpaDeX), which demonstrated docking and undocking capabilities and made India the fourth country to achieve the feat.The Prime Minister also highlighted India's growing human spaceflight capabilities, noting that an Indian astronaut had travelled to the International Space Station (ISS) and conducted experiments that would contribute to the country's Gaganyaan programme.SPACE TECHNOLOGY FOR EVERYDAY LIFEModi stressed that India's space programme was not limited to scientific exploration but was also delivering practical benefits to citizens.He pointed to the use of satellite technology in providing fishermen with alerts about approaching cyclones and tracking their movements, helping improve maritime safety.Satellite-based systems are also being used to track trains in real time, through collaboration between ISRO and Indian Railways, improving railway operations and passenger information services.The Prime Minister said these applications demonstrated how investments in advanced space technology could translate into tangible public benefits.PRIVATE SECTOR AND YOUNG INNOVATORS TAKE CENTRE STAGEModi also highlighted the opening up of India's space sector to private participation, saying it had created new opportunities for entrepreneurs, startups and young innovators.Young Indians are now developing rockets, building satellites and working on technologies that were previously largely restricted to government space agencies.He also underlined the importance of nurturing scientific curiosity among school students through initiatives such as Atal Tinkering Labs, which encourage innovation and hands-on experimentation.The Prime Minister further referred to the One Nation One Subscription initiative, which aims to provide students, researchers and academic institutions access to international research journals and scientific publications.Modi said expanding access to scientific knowledge and research infrastructure was essential to building India's future innovation ecosystem.His remarks reinforced the broader message that India's expanding scientific and space capabilities must translate into opportunities, knowledge and solutions for society.- Ends
